architectural_units.name: User
architectural_units.description: The end user of the system, including business users, support staff, and administrators.

architectural_units.name: Leader
architectural_units.description: Central routing service that manages traffic and communications between external services and internal microservices.

architectural_units.name: Portal
architectural_units.description: Centralized interface for accessing applications and hosting frontend binaries.

architectural_units.name: Access Control
architectural_units.description: Service responsible for user authentication, authorization, and role management.

architectural_units.name: Communication Log
architectural_units.description: Service that records all system communications for traceability and auditing.

architectural_units.name: Scheduler
architectural_units.description: Service for planning and automating system tasks and maintenance.

architectural_units.name: Amazon RDS
architectural_units.description: Managed relational database service used for data persistence.

architectural_units.name: Amazon Web Services
architectural_units.description: Cloud provider hosting the system infrastructure.
Connection between User and Internet.

architectural_units.name: Internet
architectural_units.description: Network medium for user access.
Connection between Internet and Portal Gateway.
Connection between Portal Gateway and Leader.
Connection between Leader and internal microservices.
Connection between internal microservices and Amazon RDS.

architectural_units.name: Presentation Layer
architectural_units.description: Frontend layer handling user interface and interactions.

architectural_units.name: Business Logic Layer
architectural_units.description: Service layer implementing domain rules and processing.

architectural_units.name: Data Access Layer
architectural_units.description: Repository layer interacting with the database.

architectural_units.name: Domain Layer
architectural_units.description: Layer defining internal data models.

architectural_units.name: Contract Layer
architectural_units.description: Layer containing DTOs and Mappers for API communication.

architectural_units.name: View
architectural_units.description: Frontend component responsible for display and user input capture.

architectural_units.name: ViewModel
architectural_units.description: Frontend component managing behavior, data processing, and service orchestration.

architectural_units.name: Model
architectural_units.description: Frontend component defining data contracts.

architectural_units.name: Angular
architectural_units.description: Frontend framework used for building the SPA.

architectural_units.name: Spring Boot
architectural_units.description: Backend framework for building microservices.

architectural_units.name: REST API
architectural_units.description: Communication protocol used between client and server.

architectural_units.name: HTTP
architectural_units.description: Protocol for message exchange.

architectural_units.name: JSON
architectural_units.description: Data format for communication.

patterns.name: Microservices
patterns.description: The system is divided into small, independent, and autonomous services where each microservice is responsible for a specific functionality and communicates with others via messaging systems.

patterns.name: Cloud Architecture
patterns.description: The application is designed, deployed, and executed using cloud computing services (AWS) instead of local or physical servers, allowing for scalability, availability, and accessibility.

patterns.name: Client-Server
patterns.description: The application organizes code into two distinct components: the client, which formulates service requests, and the server, which receives, processes, and returns responses.

patterns.name: MVVM (Model-View-ViewModel)
patterns.description: Used in the Angular frontend, this pattern separates the user interface (View) from the logic and data processing (ViewModel) and the data contract (Model).

patterns.name: Layered Architecture
patterns.description: The server (backend) organizes code into layers to separate responsibilities: presentation, business logic, data access, domain, and contract layers.

patterns.name: Single-Page Application (SPA)
patterns.description: The client is developed as a Single-Page Application that renders dynamic views and manages internal navigation without reloading the page.
